subject: Pilot extension options — orchestrated bucket vs time extension
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita@brightpath.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightPath Procurement <procurement@brightpath.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot extension request + packaging question

Marcus — thanks again for the run so far. Our engineers hit a hard stop this week while validating end-to-end latency under a steady concurrency profile. We have two asks: one, can we get a short extension on the pilot (2 weeks) so we can finish the integration tests; two, we need clarity on pricing if we go beyond the original timebox: is Redwood prepared to offer an "orchestrated bucket" (a burst bucket + sustained bucket) instead of pure calendar extension?

High level constraints:
- We can commit to a predictable sustained baseline (approx 20k tokens/day) for those two weeks but need burst capacity up to 5x for short windows.
- Procurement will prefer a single amendment vs multiple invoices.

Can you outline what packaging/pricing Cambridge would look like for (A) a straight time extension with credits, vs (B) an orchestrated bucket (sustained + burst) with a single amendment? We attached a short SOW draft and the usage sample.

Thanks —
Anita
Head of Integrations, BrightPath Analytics

Attachments: SOW_BrightPath_v2.pdf (draft), usage_sample_June.csv (referenced)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Rao <anita@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot extension request + packaging question

Thanks Anita — great context, and glad the integration is moving. I pulled Connor and Laura in here since this touches billing and SOW. High level options below, with the pros/cons and a suggested recommended path. I also attached a quick pricing model (pricing_model_v3.xlsx) to illustrate numbers.

Option A — Timebox extension with credits (simple amendment)
- Add 14 calendar days to the pilot; we issue X credits redeemable against all inference usage.
- Pricing: credits priced at the same blended rate you have today, with a 5% extension discount if signed within 5 business days.
- Pros: Fast to execute, single-line amendment. Cons: Less flexible if you spike beyond estimated tokens; potential for early depletion and mid-period interruptions.

Option B — Orchestrated bucket (sustained + burst)
- Define a sustained bucket (committed tokens per day for the extension window) + a separate burst pool (token credits reserved for spikes). Billing performed as a single amendment with clear drawdown rules.
- Pricing: sustained tokens billed at a lower committed rate; burst tokens billed at a higher one but with a capped effective rate (we can cap daily burst spend to avoid runaway cost).
- Pros: Smooths cost predictability and protects you from temporary spikes. Cons: Requires a short operational attachment in the SOW (drawdown rules, fair-use trigger thresholds).

Recommendation: For your stated profile (steady 20k tokens/day + intermittent 5x spikes), Option B reduces your expected overage by ~18% in our model and keeps procurement happy with a single amendment. If you'd like, Connor can propose the exact strike (sustained/burst split) based on the attached usage sample.

Next steps I propose:
1) We propose a sustained bucket of 20k tokens/day for 14 days + a burst pool of 500k tokens (sizable but bounded).
2) Laura will work the single amendment language so procurement has one invoice and one DocuSign flow.
3) We sign the amendment and provision the burst bucket; we can turn on monitoring/tracing hooks in the Console so you can see drawdown in real time.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through numbers tomorrow.

—Marcus
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
Contact: +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: pricing_model_v3.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Rao <anita@brightpath.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot extension request + packaging question

Anita — looping in procurement language and a single-amendment approach. Draft summary of amendment clauses (excerpt):

- Amendment term: 14 calendar days starting on the effective date signed via DocuSign.
- Billing: Single line item for Sustained Bucket (committed tokens) + single line item for Burst Pool (pre-paid credits). Burst draws reduce the pre-paid pool; unused burst credits expire at term end but can be converted to a one-time credit toward future hosted usage at 50% of face value (in case you want flexibility).
- Fair use & protection: Burst triggers defined as >3x daily sustained average for two consecutive hours; Redwood reserves the right to throttle if abuse detected; mitigation path includes automatic alerting and manual unthrottle within 30 minutes on request.
- Approval path: Procurement signs the amendment; commercial approval executed by Redwood AE + Revenue Ops.

Pricing note: We can offer a 7% volume discount on the sustained bucket for this pilot amendment (one-time concession) if the amendment is executed by EOD Friday. That concession nets BrightPath roughly ~4% off projected spend vs the base model in the workbook.

I'll draft the amendment and route via DocuSign once you confirm which option you prefer.

Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: amendment_excerpt.docx (sent internally)

From: Anita Rao <anita@brightpath.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightPath Procurement <procurement@brightpath.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot extension request + packaging question

Thanks Marcus and Laura — this is really helpful. BrightPath is inclined to take Option B (orchestrated bucket) given the spike risk. A couple of clarifications before we sign:

- Can you make the burst conversion option 60% (instead of 50%)? Finance argues we should get more value for unused pre-paid burst credits.
- Can you confirm the cap on daily burst spend so we can model worst-case?
- Lastly, can the amendment include a clause that the sustain rate is locked for the 14-day term and will not be repriced mid-term?

If you can update the amendment excerpt with those three points and route via DocuSign, procurement will aim to sign within 48 hours. We appreciate the quick turnaround on this.

—Anita
Head of Integrations, BrightPath Analytics
